items.summary_raw:
Medicine, food and other supplies are the urgent priority. But the rising risks from shrinking glaciers must be faced too

Thousands of people in Nepal and Tibet are in desperate need of emergency assistance following Wednesday’s disaster. With 360 people confirmed dead, more than 1,300 others are still missing as search and rescue operations continue. The precise sequence of events linking glacier collapse to flash floods is yet to be confirmed. But there is no doubting the enormous destructive power of the brown torrent that can be seen on video clips surging down the steeply sided Himalayan valleys, sweeping away everyone and everything in its path.

Testimony from survivors about terrifying near-escapes and losses is reminiscent of previous disasters, including the 2004 tsunami. The human cost among the less well off will be more people regularly choosing whether to skip meals, ignore other bills or stay cold this winter.

items.title: Germany's far-right AfD pledged to remove refugee and disabled children from mainstream schools if it wins the Saxony-Anhalt regional election on September 6.  The party's manifest…
items.summary_raw: Germany's far-right AfD pledged to remove refugee and disabled children from mainstream schools if it wins the Saxony-Anhalt regional election on September 6.  The party's manifesto calls the "inclusion experiment failed" and says refugee children should be educated separately "to reinforce the message that their stay in Germany is only temporary."   Islamic education would not be offered as "Islam is not part of Germany."  The AfD also plans to expand Russian language teaching and reinstate school exchanges with Russia, citing cultural ties from the East German era.  The AfD leads polls heading into the election.   It would need over 40% to form the first wholly AfD government in German history.

items.title: Trump Has Submitted Civil Nuclear Agreement With Saudi Arabia to Congress for Review
items.summary_raw: WASHINGTON (AP) — President Donald Trump has submitted to Congress for review an agreement with Saudi Arabia aimed at bolstering the kingdom's civilian nuclear program, but continues to insist that it won't move forward if Saudi Arabia doesn't normalize relations with Israel, according to a Trump administration official. The classified document was submitted to Capitol Hill on Monday as required by the Atomic Energy Act, according to the administration official, a congressional aide, and two others familiar with the matter. All four spoke on condition of anonymity because they were not authorized to comment publicly on the classified matter. The agreement was signedlast month in Washington by U.S. Energy Secretary Chris Wright and his Saudi counterpart. But the next day, Trump announced he was requiring the Saudis to normalize relations with Israel through the Abraham Accords as part of the pact — raising doubts that the agreement would come to fruition. Neither the administration official nor the others familiar with the matter would comment on whether Trump's call for the Saudis to join the accords is detailed in the classified document submitted for the congressional review.<

items.title: Groups sue Trump’s EPA over fast-track approval of toxic datacenter chemicals
items.summary_raw:
Exposure to two compounds approved can result in ‘sudden death’ and range of other serious health risks, lawsuit warns

The Trump administration has approved two new datacenter chemicals to which exposure can result in “sudden death” and a range of other serious health risks, like cancer, eye corrosion, neurological damage and reproductive harm, a new lawsuit warns.

The two compounds approved by the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) for import and immediate use in facilities across the US are photoacid generators that also appear to be Pfas “forever chemicals”, though it is unclear because much of the EPA documents are redacted. Some Pfas are commonly used in the production of semiconductors.

This article was amended on 26 August 2026. A previous version said the EPA concedes that the chemicals present an “unreasonable risk” to workers. It has been updated to say the chemicals may present an unreasonable risk.

items.title: France is pushing to limit Ukraine's ability to buy non-European military equipment with EU loan money, seeking to steer the €60 billion defense portion of the EU's €90 billion sup…
items.summary_raw: France is pushing to limit Ukraine's ability to buy non-European military equipment with EU loan money, seeking to steer the €60 billion defense portion of the EU's €90 billion support package toward European and French producers.  Ukraine has secured two exemptions so far: one for Chinese drone components and another for US Patriot interceptor missiles.   France wants these exemptions to be temporary, with European suppliers replacing foreign ones as production ramps up.  Nine EU countries including Germany, Sweden, and Poland pushed back, calling for Ukraine to have "maximum flexibility to procure the equipment it urgently needs."  France has a clear commercial interest: its Franco-Italian SAMP/T system is Europe's closest alternative to the US Patriot.  Source: Euronews

The war has crippled Qatar’s LNG lifeline, with damage at Ras Laffan and severe disruptions through the Strait of Hormuz. Qatar is reported to have lost roughly $24 billion in gas sales during the major disruption.

Doha has responded with deep budget cuts, cutting some government spending by 30% and overseas aid by roughly 85%.

Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi said in a televised interview on Tuesday that the Strait of Hormuz remains closed despite a temporary transit agreement with Oman.

“America and other countries should know that the Strait of Hormuz will not be opened except through Iranian arrangements,” Gharibabadi said, adding that Iran remains “in a state of war”.

Gharibabadi says Iran and Oman have held talks over the past 40 days on a transit arrangement through the waterway, agreeing on a temporary route seven miles (11 kilometres) wide, with the entry point and part of the exit route running through Iranian territorial waters.

Membership includes roughly 55 figures from economics, tech, and policy, including Nobel laureates, the Shopify and Klarna founders, former Estonian president Ilves, and FT editor Roula Khalaf.  Critics have already noted the irony: a group advocating European competitiveness is registered in Switzerland and hosted its website entirely on American infrastructure.

The datacenters are often sources of nitrogen oxide, which helps form ozone, carbon monoxide and heavy metals, among other pollutants.

items.summary_raw:
There has been a 76% increase in under-construction gas-fired projects amid ‘frenzy’ to build more datacenters

The US has surged ahead of China in the building of new gas-fired power generation, largely to feed a boom in artificial intelligence (AI) that is adding vast amounts of planet-heating emissions, a new analysis has found.

For decades, China’s rapid economic growth has seen it outpace the US in the addition of new gas power generation but a recent “frenzy” in datacenter construction for AI has reversed this, said Global Energy Monitor (Gem) in its new report.

items.summary_raw: Israel is planning to expand its military capabilities in space, including eventually striking targets on Earth from orbit.  Defense Minister Israel Katz says Israel wants to be first to develop a true space-to-ground attack capability. The broader plan also includes better satellites, encrypted communications, cyberwarfare and missile defense.  One concept discussed is the U.S. “Rods from God” idea: satellites dropping massive tungsten rods at extreme speed, producing bunker-busting impacts without nuclear explosives. The physics are possible, but cost, weight and effectiveness remain major obstacles.  Israel is considering roughly 16 billion shekels ($5.4 billion) in space investment over a decade, though funding is not yet assured.  Source: Haaretz

The climate damage caused by developing the Rosebank and Jackdaw oil and gas fields under consideration by the UK government would destroy their economic benefits many times over, according to an analysis.

It estimates the economic damage caused by the carbon pollution from the oil and gas produced would be between £119bn and £336bn in the coming decades, compared with the £28.7bn in value to the UK estimated by Adura, the fossil fuel company promoting the new fields.

Trump unleashes swathe sanctions on Iran 'enablers'

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on Monday announced a new wave of sanctions against Iran and its "enablers", towards what he described as an "asphyxiation of this regime" amid the standoff in the Strait of Hormuz.

"Iran now faces a very clear choice, with only two paths before them: complete global isolation and a subsistence economy, or a path back to normalcy with an opportunity to rejoin the global economy," Bessent told reporters in Washington, DC. 

It remains unclear how "a path to normalcy" may work, given the Trump administration has only ever tightened sanctions on Iran since its first iteration in the White House in 2017.

items.title: At least 35,000 excess deaths recorded in Europe’s back-to-back heatwaves
items.summary_raw:
True figure likely to be much higher as it only covers about half of continent and does not include August totals

At least 35,000 more people died during Europe’s four record-breaking, back-to-back heatwaves this summer than would normally be expected, according to incomplete figures from barely half the continent.

Excess mortality in three of the EU’s larger countries – Germany, France and Spain – alone has already exceeded 25,000, according to the provisional national figures, and experts say the toll will rise significantly once August totals are consolidated.

The ministry accused the two lawmakers of having “consistently acted against Israel”, including by calling for international legal proceedings against Israelis.

It also accused them of spreading “false accusations against Israel”, including allegations of genocide, deliberate starvation and the intentional targeting of children and medical personnel.

items.summary_raw:
Average sea surface temperature outside polar regions was 21.1C on Saturday, latest data finds

The world’s oceans were hotter than ever previously recorded on Saturday, according to the latest data.

The average surface temperature was 21.1C, with the rising marine heat a stark indicator of the climate crisis. More than 90% of the heat trapped by carbon dioxide from fossil fuel burning enters the oceans.

items.title: This is not a natural calamity: it is being done to us knowingly
items.summary_raw:
Global heating is an outrage, not a tragedy. We deserve the facts about the climate crisis – I choose the Guardian because it’s one of the few places left to share them honestly

  • Climate campaign 2026: help us reach 30,000 acts of support

Well, there’s no getting around it now. What many of us once feared has become a reality.

The dangerous conditions climate scientists long warned of have become our common, if deeply unwelcome, experience, and season by season, our acquaintance with disorder and extremities deepens. In both hemispheres, wildfires rage right into our cities and incinerate entire neighbourhoods. Marine heatwaves are bleaching corals and cooking seagrasses on a global scale. This northern summer has brought temperatures most Europeans associate with the Australian desert. Heat events in Europe have paralysed whole countries, destroyed infrastructure and killed citizens in their thousands.

The technology could also be used in semi-solid and solid-state batteries in the future.

items.summary_raw:
Carbon capture and storage could make the Rosebank site compatible with UK net zero commitments – if its owners are willing to pay the price

The British government must soon decide whether it should give consent to two oil and gasfields, Rosebank in the North Atlantic and Jackdaw in the North Sea. Amid both insecurity of energy supplies and deadly evidence of the climate crisis, the prime minister, Andy Burnham, is facing pressure from the oil and gas industry and unions on one side, and environmentalists on the other.

Labour’s manifesto commitment not to approve new drilling licences offers little help, because the fields already have licences, granted by the previous Conservative government in 2022 and 2023. But last year, Edinburgh’s court of session ruled that the environmental impact assessments on which this decision relied were unlawful. items.title: Former CIA officer describes Aipac's rise to political power
items.summary_raw:
Former CIA officer describes Aipac's rise to political power

Former CIA officer John Kiriakou and journalist Tucker Carlson sharply discuss the power of the Israel lobby in Washington, including Aipac's controversial rise, Israel’s attack on the USS Liberty in 1967, and Israel’s involvement in the assassination of U.S. President John F. Kennedy.

The two discuss how the Johnson administration protected Israel after the attack on the American ship and punished surviving crew members for speaking about what happened.

According to their discussion, Israel attacked the USS Liberty again roughly 45 minutes after the initial attack.
“There’s no question they tried to sink it.”

They also discuss JFK’s confrontation with Israel over its nuclear programme and Israel’s involvement in Kennedy’s assassination

ATHENS (AP) — Migrants clashed with police at a detention center in northern Greece and cut through a perimeter fence, with 35 escaping before authorities recaptured about half of them, officials said Sunday. Greece is a key entry point for migrants into Europe, and migration is a hot-button issue in the country. Greece’s conservative government has been toughening its migration policies. Police reinforcements were called late on Saturday to the temporary accommodation center for asylum seekers in Sintiki, a few kilometers (miles) from the Bulgarian border, after migrants threw rocks at guards, according to police. The facility houses around 450 people who are placed there while their asylum applications are processed, which can be a protracted procedure. Police special forces responded with flash grenades during the clashes, which officials said lasted until the early hours of Sunday. Police said they arrested 17 of the migrants who had escaped, while searches continued for around 18 others. An additional five migrants were injured and taken to hospital.

"The Iranians cannot be trusted at the negotiating table," he added.

We have one gas supply line that passes through the territory of Poland to Europe. And a second line was prepared, also through the territory of Poland. This was partly because, first of all, certain economic advantages as a transit country are lost.   And secondly, Poland would receive less—which is exactly what happened—it began to receive less income from the transit of our hydrocarbons.

items.title: NEW: Russia is quietly running nationwide mobilization readiness exercises testing its ability to house, feed, and arm a large influx of new recruits.  In one exercise in July, mil…
items.summary_raw: NEW: Russia is quietly running nationwide mobilization readiness exercises testing its ability to house, feed, and arm a large influx of new recruits.  In one exercise in July, military officers flew from St. Petersburg to Kaliningrad to oversee concrete mobilization planning for the exclave's residents.   Similar tests are taking place across the country "in case the call is made."  No decision has been taken by the Kremlin.   Unlike the chaotic 2022 mobilization, Russia now has an electronic register of military-age men that would allow a more gradual process.   Speculation centers on a possible call-up after Russia's September parliamentary elections.  Source: WSJ

items.title: Visioner ✈️🇺🇦 Ukraine plans to build much of the infrastructure needed to operate its future European fighter fleet at home, with Gripen and Rafale agreements providing for the loc…
items.summary_raw: Visioner ✈️🇺🇦 Ukraine plans to build much of the infrastructure needed to operate its future European fighter fleet at home, with Gripen and Rafale agreements providing for the localization of production and maintenance inside Ukraine.  According to the Ukrainian Air Force’s Central Command, contracts covering the future delivery of Swedish Gripen and French Rafale fighters include provisions for establishing production and repair capabilities on Ukrainian territory. Ukraine has already contracted an initial 16 newly built Gripen E fighters, while its broader plans envision a significantly larger fleet of European combat aircraft.   The localization component could be almost as important as the aircraft themselves. Ukraine is seeking not merely to purchase Western fighters, but to build a domestic ecosystem capable of maintaining, repairing and eventually participating in their production. In the long term, that would reduce dependence on foreign maintenance facilities while integrating Ukraine much more deeply into Europe’s defense-industrial base.  See the latest updates with us: @visionergeo tweet

items.title: China’s Type 004 aircraft carrier is rapidly taking shape at Dalian, with new satellite imagery showing a more complete bow and a hull already around 320 meters long.  The stronges…
items.summary_raw: China’s Type 004 aircraft carrier is rapidly taking shape at Dalian, with new satellite imagery showing a more complete bow and a hull already around 320 meters long.  The strongest open-source assessment is that it will be China’s first nuclear-powered carrier, with imagery reportedly showing two reactor containment structures.  Expected features include EMALS catapults, a 90–100+ aircraft air wing, and a displacement potentially above 110,000 tons.  The carrier is expected to be substantially larger and more capable than Fujian, likely around 110,000–120,000 tons, with a final length approaching or exceeding the U.S. Gerald R. Ford-class.  Current estimates suggest four catapults, compared with three on Fujian, and an air wing potentially exceeding 90 aircraft, including J-35 stealth fighters, J-15T carrier fighters, KJ-600 airborne early-warning aircraft, helicopters, and eventually combat drones.  A launch could come as early as 2027, followed by several years of fitting-out and sea trials, with entry into service around 2030.  SOURCE

items.title: ⚡️ The United States Navy unveiled a new air-to-air missile named AIM-424. This missile, despite its recent public announcement, is almost ready for operational deployment, which m…
items.summary_raw: ⚡️ The United States Navy unveiled a new air-to-air missile named AIM-424. This missile, despite its recent public announcement, is almost ready for operational deployment, which means its project has been secretly underway for years. The missile is 411 centimeters long, 34 centimeters in diameter, and weighs 680 kilograms, with a range of approximately 460 kilometers. In terms of weight and size, this missile is slightly larger than the Russian R-37M and can be said to offer a similar increase in range. However, its main advantage is its ability to be carried in the internal bay of the F-35, a feat that the R-37M has not yet achieved. The US, which until a year ago only had two operational air-to-air missiles, the AIM-120 and AIM-9X, has added three new air-to-air missiles to its arsenal in the past year: the AIM-260, which is AMRAAM-sized with a 250-kilometer range and was recently introduced, and the massive 900-kilogram AIM-174 missile, which has a range of approximately 500 kilometers.

That is broadly consistent with the direction of current U.S. policy toward Damascus. items.summary_raw:
Surge in proposals follows Labour’s lifting of de facto ban, with about 45 plans submitted in the year to March

Plans for new onshore windfarms in England have reached their highest annual level in a decade, after the government overturned the Conservatives’ de facto ban in 2015.

About 45 applications for new onshore windfarms were submitted in the year to March,according to a Guardian analysis of government data.

items.summary_raw: OSINTdefender The U.S. Navy has publicly disclosed a previously unannounced AIM-424 Long Range Air-to-Air Missile (LRAAM), also known as the "Malice", revealing the weapon mounted inside the internal weapons bay of an F-35C Lightning II with an AIM-120 AMRAAM mounted on the bay door. The Navy describes the AIM-424 as its next-generation, long range air to air missile, intended to give Navy and Marine Corps aviators greater capability against advanced threats.  The internal carriage is particularly significant. Rather than simply adding another externally carried long-range missile, the AIM-424 appears to have been designed around the F-35's limited internal weapons-bay dimensions, allowing the aircraft to retain its low-observable configuration while carrying a substantially longer-range air-to-air weapon.  The missile is still associated with testing and development, and the Navy has released few technical details regarding its range, seeker, propulsion or intended employment. The available imagery does, however, show the AIM-424 being evaluated on both the F-35C and F/A-18E/F, indicating that the weapon is being considered across the Navy's carrier aviation force. items.title: BIG: Qatar slashed government budgets by up to 30% and cut overseas aid by roughly 85% as the Iran war devastates its LNG-dependent economy.  Iranian strikes on Ras Laffan, the wor…
items.summary_raw: BIG: Qatar slashed government budgets by up to 30% and cut overseas aid by roughly 85% as the Iran war devastates its LNG-dependent economy.  Iranian strikes on Ras Laffan, the world's largest LNG hub, cut export capacity by 17%, with full recovery expected to take 3-5 years.   The effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz has further crippled exports.   The IMF projects Qatar's GDP will contract 8.6% in 2026.  Goldman Sachs estimates Qatar and Kuwait are losing $1.5-2 billion per week in energy revenue.   Qatar is drawing on its roughly $500 billion sovereign wealth fund to maintain liquidity but is "seriously contemplating" further cuts if the crisis continues.  Source: FT

items.title: Wildfires Continue in Greece, Bringing Destruction and Tragedy
items.summary_raw:
ATHENS – Water-dropping aircraft and ground forces managed to bring under control three wildfires in mainland Greece on August 20, as about half the country faced a category-3 risk on a 5-notch scale. Earlier in the week two wildfires broke out nearly simultaneously on the island of Salamina near Piraeus. The situation turned tragic, with two people, believed to be an elderly couple, found dead in the Peristeria area. Eight people suffered burns, while there were reports of homes being completely engulfed in flames. On Aug. 20 the Fire Service said four aircraft flew sorties to help 35 firefighters contain a blaze near the village of Kremasti in the Sparta region of the southern Peloponnese. Two more wildfires coursing through forest and farmland near the villages of Palamas in the central Karditsa region and Paralimni in the northern Serres area were brought under control. For Aug. 20, civil protection authorities have set most of the country on a category-3 risk level, including nearly the entire Peloponnese, central Greece with the Greater Athens region and the island of Evia, northwestern Greece, Crete and nearly all the Aegean Sea islands.

items.title: Trump Is Destroying America’s Greatest Strategic Asset
items.summary_raw:
For eighty years, America's greatest strategic advantage was not its aircraft carriers, nuclear weapons, economy or even the dollar. It was its allies. Russia has satellites and dependents. China has partners and clients. Iran has proxies. America built something none of them could reproduce: alliances with countries that actually wanted to be our allies. They trusted us because, despite our mistakes and occasional arrogance, they believed Washington would ultimately take their interests into account.

items.title: NEW: Germany is planning nearly €12 billion for a new long-range strike arsenal to deter Russia.  The four-layered plan starts with cheap, mass-producible cruise missiles as early …
items.summary_raw: NEW: Germany is planning nearly €12 billion for a new long-range strike arsenal to deter Russia.  The four-layered plan starts with cheap, mass-producible cruise missiles as early as 2027, including Ukraine's FP-5 Flamingo with 3,000 km range at roughly one-fifth the cost of a Tomahawk.   US Tomahawk missiles with Typhon launchers follow by end of the decade.   The most expensive element is a joint UK-Germany program developing stealth cruise missiles and a hypersonic glide weapon exceeding 2,000 km range, targeted for the mid-2030s.  Documents describe the capability as enabling strikes "far into the rear area of an adversary" while staying "below the nuclear threshold."   Source: Politico

items.summary_raw: ⚡️ 🔻Global oil prices rose on Friday following US President Donald Trump's threat to impose economic sanctions on countries that provide assistance to Iran. Brent crude oil reached $94.39 per barrel, an increase of 61 cents per barrel. US West Texas Intermediate crude also rose to $87.06, an increase of 23 cents. According to a Reuters report, Brent crude rose by more than 6%, and US crude rose by more than 5% this week. Analysts say that the new US threat to increase economic pressure on Iran and its trading partners has heightened concerns about declining oil supplies in the coming weeks. At the same time, shipping traffic through the Strait of Hormuz remains significantly below its usual levels. Data from Kepler, a company specializing in ship tracking, indicates that only seven commercial vessels crossed the Strait of Hormuz on Thursday, a figure that represents half the number recorded the previous day. Before the start of the American attacks on Iran at the end of February, about one-fifth of the world's supply of oil and liquefied natural gas passed through the Strait of Hormuz.

items.title: Wildfire Breaks out in Thanos on the North Aegean Island of Limnos
items.summary_raw:
MYRINA – A state of alert was declared on Friday, August 21 on the island of Limnos in the northern Aegean Sea after a wildfire broke out in the Thanos area, on the southern side of the island, prompting a major mobilization of the Fire Service and Coast Guard. The fire broke out at around 2:30 PM in low vegetation and, as it spread, it became necessary to evacuate residents and beachgoers from areas near the fire front. A particularly large-scale operation took place at Thanos Beach, where dozens of people, including elderly people and children, had become trapped. Under the coordination of the Operations Center of the Hellenic Coast Guard, a total of 59 people were evacuated by sea and safely transported to the port of Myrina.

The post Wildfire Breaks out in Thanos on the North Aegean Island of Limnos appeared first on The National Herald.

items.title: Where Turkey Is Heading in the Aegean: Maritime Parks and the Expansion of Ankara’s Territorial Claims
items.summary_raw:
ATHENS. Turkey’s latest moves in the Aegean are not simply another episode in the long chain of Greek-Turkish disputes. Ankara’s successive challenges to Greece’s marine parks, its Maritime Spatial Planning framework and, most recently, the Special Spatial Planning Framework for Renewable Energy Sources point to a more systematic effort to extend its longstanding claims into every new activity involving the maritime space. The most troubling aspect is not so much Ankara’s reaction to Greek initiatives as the revival of its “gray zones” theory. Turkey’s Foreign Ministry, followed by its Defense Ministry, referred to “geographical formations whose sovereignty has not been transferred to Greece through international treaties.” Athens responded in unusually strong terms, calling the claims “unfounded, completely unacceptable and rejected,” and stressing that the status of sovereignty in the Aegean has been definitively established by international treaties.

items.title: Trump Warns of ‘Economic D-Day’ Against Iran, but Tehran Is Well Acquainted With Sanctions
items.summary_raw:
NEW YORK (AP) — Nearing the six-month mark of the Iran war and facing diminishing stockpiles of key weapons, the Trump administration is touting a crushing financial campaign against Tehran, promising an “economic D-Day” against a country that has so far withstood nearly five decades of punishing American sanctions. With sparse details, President Donald Trump announced this week that the U.S. would be imposing an “unprecedented” level of economic warfare and isolation on Iran, aiming to force its leadership to cave to demands to end its nuclear program and fully reopen the crucial Strait of Hormuz to oil and natural gas tankers. It reflects the dire reality Trump faces with an increasingly unpopular war he can't seem to end just months before pivotal midterm elections that will decide whether his Republican Party keeps control of Congress. Whether out of desperation or strategy, the president is refocusing America's might on bringing Iran to its knees through an accelerated sanctions campaign against one of the most economically penalized countries in the world.

items.title: Proposed London datacentre will have annual carbon footprint of 27,000 flights to New York
items.summary_raw:
Exclusive: Planning documents show datacentre in North Ockendon would be incompatible with UK net zero targets

A “hyperscale” datacentre in outer London would generate more than 1m tonnes of carbon dioxide a year, equivalent to the carbon footprint of 27,000 flights from London to New York, planning documents show.

The East Havering Data Centre Campus (EHDCC) in North Ockendon would be one of the largest datacentres in Europe if approved by Havering council, using 218 hectares of green belt to run servers and data storage systems for AI and cloud computing. Its developer, Digital Reef, has described the scheme as “a unique opportunity to create a sustainable datacentre campus of the future”.
